The JDK 25 reference's RAM is bimodal on this runner -- run 37108550136 measured it at 948-1801 MB across rounds while ParparVM stayed at 794-872 MB -- so a run's median ratio lands anywhere from 0.555x to 0.907x with unchanged VM code, and the global 15% tolerance around 0.803x failed that run as IMPROVED at 0.565x.

PR #5883: valueEscape time on this CPU is bimodal on the runner, not moved by this branch. Run 37135467315 read 0.216x against 0.132x: rounds 0.216, 0.215, 0.227, 0.223 and 0.132 (ParparVM 1.5-1.6 ms, then 0.9 ms; JDK 25 6.9-7.0 ms), so the SAME binary measured the old baseline exactly in round 5. Each round is the min of 5 reps timed with nanoTime, which on Windows reads GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime at 1 us, so 0.9 against 1.5 ms is not clock quantization. Elsewhere this branch's valueEscape equals master's on every row: Linux Xeon 8370C, the same Ice Lake model on Linux, 0.133x against base 0.133x; Windows AMD Family 25 Model 1 0.100x-0.101x (8 runs) against 0.100x (master 3, other branches 13); Neoverse-N2 0.507x-0.508x (13) against 0.508x (3); Windows arm64 D49 0.761x-0.762x (8) against 0.761x (3). This CPU has no other run on record (the 0.132x row came from one run of #5903's code, now expired), so the row is recalibrated from the two run medians that exist, 0.132x and 0.216x: baseline at their median with a tolerance from their spread, which passes either mode. A real regression on this CPU must now exceed 0.244x.
